card: This PR modifies wallet fee bumping to ensure a replacement transaction does not receive an nLockTime earlier than the transaction it replaces. Anti-fee-sniping randomly backdates locktimes by up to 99 blocks roughly 10% of the time, which can cause bumpfee to produce a replacement with a lower locktime than the original. This regression acts as an on-chain fingerprint identifying Bitcoin Core and Electrum wallets. An empirical survey cited in the PR found 200 to 300 backdated replacements per week out of over one million RBF transactions.
changed_since_previous: The implementation approach remains the same; handling for edge cases where the chain tip is stale or lagging behind minimum_height was refined and tested.
evidence: Author's empirical survey in PR description: across over 1,000,000 RBF transactions between May 2025 and June 2026, roughly 200 to 300 replacements backdated locktimes per week (under 2% of replacements), uniquely fingerprinting them.
problem: Bitcoin Core's anti-fee-sniping mechanism randomly backdates transaction locktimes by up to 99 blocks approximately 10% of the time. When bumping fees on an existing transaction, this random roll can result in a replacement transaction with an older locktime than the original, creating an unnatural on-chain pattern that fingerprints the wallet as Bitcoin Core or Electrum.

risk.why: A flaw in anti-fee-sniping locktime bounds could set an invalid locktime or lock a transaction to a future height, causing fee bumps to fail or transactions to remain unbroadcastable.

scope_notes: Touches transaction generation in the wallet (spend.cpp and feebumper.cpp), adding a minimum_height parameter to DiscourageFeeSniping.
summary: Prevents wallet fee-bumped transactions from receiving an nLockTime earlier than the transaction they replace. When replacing a transaction via bumpfee, the wallet records the original locktime in CCoinControl and uses it as a floor in DiscourageFeeSniping so random anti-fee-sniping backdating cannot decrease the locktime.
